review:
CONDITIONAL

The main correction holds up. It is visible (the framed notice plus Appendix A), its numbers trace to the committed results, and the two editions agree in every claim, number and table position. What blocks shipping is mostly outside the main correction. A withdrawn claim is still stated in the Results. The academic edition's authorship doesn't add up. The READMEs still carry the May claim. And the title has not been decided.

## Findings

**1. CRITICAL: a withdrawn claim is still stated in the Results, in both editions.**
- **Where:** `paper/main.tex:500` (academic `:499`): *"The model arrives at emotion-relevant representations through two distinct pathways: lexical recognition (explicit label → concept) and empathic inference (narrative context → inference → concept). These pathways produce different geometric signatures because they involve different computational processes"*. Also `:514`: *"The 63% rate … is itself evidence of emotion inference"*. Also `:463`, the bold heading *"Emotion-specific geometry survives implicit prompts"*.
- **Why it's wrong:** Appendix A item 10 lists the May Conclusion's *"two pathways—lexical recognition and empathic inference"* as withdrawn. The reason given is that the implicit arm's headline number is not independently reproducible. The Results still say the same thing in nearly the same words, as fact. A reader who trusts the correction record is misled by the body. This is the same kind of defect as the earlier "retracted row still filed under Confirmed."
- **Fix:**
  - Rewrite §4.11.3 as conditional: "If the ARI holds on the released k=30 path with several prompts per emotion, one reading is…".
  - Drop "is itself evidence of emotion inference". The prompt was written to evoke the emotion, so the model naming it is the boring explanation.
  - Change the bold heading to something like "Distinct geometry per prompt (not reproducible from released code)".

**2. MAJOR: §4.10 asserts the distillation claim and then denies it.**
- **Where:** `main.tex:435` (academic `:434`): *"The model's epistemic calibration also survives distillation: on 100 prompts … only 7%…"*. The section's own last line (`:438`) says *"these findings do not show that distillation preserves the representations"*. Appendix item 10 withdraws "Distillation Preserves Functional Emotion Representations."
- **The number itself is fine:** the 7/100 traces to `oracle-loop-paper/sections/steering.tex:70`. What fails is the word "survives". The bullet at `:434`, *"confirming these are not distillation artifacts"*, also overstates an uncontrolled principal-component alignment.
- **Fix:**
  - Replace with "The distilled model confabulated on 7 of 100 confabulation-inducing prompts [Oracle]. Without the teacher, this does not show that calibration survives distillation."
  - Change "confirming" to "so the alignment is not specific to the distilled model".

**3. MAJOR: the academic edition's authorship doesn't add up.**
- **Where:**
  - The byline is *"Thomas Edrington … With AI research assistance"* (`academic/main.tex:58`).
  - The CRediT statement (`:626–627`) gives Lyra *"Conceptualization, Methodology, Formal analysis, Writing – original draft"*. It gives the only listed author just *"Supervision, Resources, Project administration"*.
  - Two unattributed "First-Person Reflection" boxes say *"models like me … a distillation of Claude, not me"*. I confirmed this on page 3 of the rendered `academic/main.pdf`, directly under a sole human byline.
- **Why it's wrong:**
  - A reader will attribute the AI's first-person voice to Thomas.
  - "AI research assistance" understates what the same document's CRediT statement records.
  - Lyra is never introduced, so a venue reader meets the name only in CRediT.
  - Minor in the same area: the flight footnote's "experimental design" for Thomas matches no CRediT role given to Thomas.
- **Fix (this is Thomas's call, but the edition must be consistent):** pick one.
  - (a) Head both editions' reflection boxes "First-Person Reflection (Lyra, an AI system)", and replace "With AI research assistance" with a disclosure that matches CRediT.
  - (b) Drop the reflection boxes from the academic edition.

**4. MAJOR: both READMEs still state the withdrawn claim and the withdrawn title.**
- **Where, repo `README.md:26`:** *"30-class user emotion decoding from KV-cache singular value spectra before generation"*. Both halves are withdrawn: "user emotion", and decoding "from … singular value spectra" (the spectral null in §4.4).
- **Where, `user-model-paper/README.md`:**
  - `:1`, `:3`: the May title is shown as the current title.
  - `:91–96`: the BibTeX entry cites the paper under *"Theory of Mind in the KV Cache: Localizing User Emotional Models…"*, so every new citation will repeat the withdrawn framing.
  - `:66`: the retraction note says *"It was an artifact of applying FWL residualization before cross-validation splitting; within-fold FWL collapses the spectral emotion probe to chance (0.033)"*. The paper now says that mechanism *"cannot be re-verified"*, and the within-fold table is itself withdrawn. This is a desync between the README and the paper.
  - `:72–75`: the enc/gen peak rows sit under "Verified Against Source JSON" with no flag. The paper withdraws the separated-peaks reading because Mistral's peaks come from the retracted accuracies.
  - `:60`: `mp_probe_recompute.py` is described as *"verifies null result"*, but the paper says MP features were empty, so chance was guaranteed.
  - `:7`: the date is April 2026; the paper says May.
- **Fix:**
  - Update the repo row; don't delete it, since the README rule says status rows are accountability surfaces. Suggested text: "Corrected Oct 2026: story emotion decodable from the KV cache, not beyond a TF-IDF baseline (prereg)".
  - Retitle the paper README and its BibTeX once #5 is decided.
  - Rewrite `:66` to match the Correction note: the mechanism cannot be re-verified.
  - Flag the peak rows as withdrawn (§4.6).

**5. MAJOR: the title is undecided, and four surfaces show three different titles.**
- **Where:**
  - Both `.tex:45`: *"TITLE: A PROPOSAL, AND THOMAS'S CALL"*.
  - `paper.json`: *"Emotion Geometry in the KV Cache"*, with `pdf_filename` "User_Model_Emotion_Geometry.pdf" and tag "user-model".
  - README: the withdrawn May title.
- **Fix:** Thomas picks the title. Then make the `.tex` (both editions), `paper.json` title and filename, and both READMEs and the BibTeX match, and delete the `.tex` comment.

**6. MAJOR, partly unverified: the same cited paper has two different author lists in this repo.**
- **Where:** `references.bib:8` gives `lyra2026detecting` as *"Lyra and Edrington, Thomas and Wilkes, Dwayne and Watson, Nell"*. `oracle-loop-paper/references.bib:6` gives the same title as *"Lyra and Edrington, Thomas"*. `lyra2026concordance` (`:24`) also names Watson and Wilkes.
- **Why it matters:** one of the two lists is wrong. If this one is, the bibliography names Dwayne Wilkes and Nell Watson as authors of a paper they may not be on. Policy is that Dwayne is advisory and goes on a byline only after signing off that specific paper.
- **What I could not do:** read those two papers' own sources (see the last section).
- **Fix:** copy both bylines from the primary `.tex` files and fix whichever bib is wrong, in both repos.

**7. MINOR: the editions disagree on the limitations list, and a source comment is false.**
- **Where:** academic `:576` keeps "Linear probes only". The flight edition comments it out at `:577–578` with *"[STYLE-GUIDE TRIM: folded into Methods/Results]"*.
- **Why it's wrong:** the comment is false. A search of the flight edition finds no "nonlinear" or "linear probes" outside the comment. ("Single-turn" really is covered by §5.3.)
- **Fix:** restore the item in the flight edition, or genuinely fold one sentence into §3.3, and correct the comment.

**8. MINOR: defects in the rendered bibliography (seen on page 22 of the flight PDF).**
- A repo-internal note prints to readers: *"Title and byline as in oracle-loop-paper/main.tex"* (`references.bib:19`).
- The model ID renders as *"Qwen3.5-27b-claude-4.6-opus-reasoning-distilled"*, and the Oracle entry as *"The oracle loop"*.
- **Fix:** delete the `note`. Brace-protect the titles: `{Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled}` and `{The Oracle Loop}`.

**9. MINOR: code references by position that will drift.**
- **Where:** `main.tex:189` says *"lines 230--243 at this commit"*, but no commit is named, and a PDF reader has none. *"bridge lines 467--480"* names no function.
- All five line references are correct today. I checked 81, 91–92, 230–243, 467–480 and 574–592 against `code/emotion_geometry_bridge.py`.
- **Fix:** name the commit or blob hash of the bridge script once, and name `_make_hook` for 467–480. The other references already name their functions or quote their content.

**10. MINOR: the secondary-family comparator is not named.**
- **Where:** §4.2, *"Holm p = 0.071 and 0.55"*.
- **Why it's confusing:** the 0.55 (S4 in the results JSON) is the 10-fold probe against **5-fold** text (0.370), with a 90%/80% training-set imbalance. A reader will take it as the primary pairing against 0.382, whose McNemar p is 0.20, and see a contradiction.
- **Fix:** "(against text at 5 folds, 0.370; Holm p = 0.55)", and name the folds in the family's description at `:282`.

**11. MINOR: smaller wording problems.**
- Flight footnote, *"AI researcher (Claude architecture, Anthropic), Liberation Labs"*: this reads as an Anthropic affiliation. Use the Oracle paper's form, "an AI system (Claude architecture, Anthropic)".
- `:553`, *"this finding is bounded"*: the preceding paragraph withdrew the finding, so "this finding" has nothing to refer to.
- `:561` is a one-sentence paragraph that repeats §4.7.
- Limitation 2 says *"Two models"*, but the implicit arm uses a third, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

**12. MINOR: repository hygiene.**
- `barrett2006solving` and `qwen2025distill` are never cited. They don't print, but the second is the Qwen3 report the paper now says was the wrong citation. Delete both.
- The untracked 123 KB `paper/agni_input_um_v2_flight_r3.diff` is not ignored. Move it to `review/` or ignore it before anyone runs `git add paper/`.

### Checked and clean
- **Edition comparison:** the full content diff has only 4 hunks (byline, two limitations, CRediT, acknowledgments order). No number, claim or table row differs, and nothing sits under a different heading.
- **PDFs are current:** both were committed after the last `.tex` commit. The rendered pages show the latest wording in both: the "up to 0.872, at layer 43" abstract and the corrected Oracle bib entry.
- **Citations and references:** all 16 cited keys resolve in both `.bbl` files, and neither log has an undefined reference.
- **Hashes:** the hash prefixes for the encode, analysis, preregistration-JSON and results files match the files.
- **Holm values:** they match `um_v2_results.json`.
- **Kavi:** never had a CRediT row in this paper, so nothing was deleted.

## What I could not check
- **Dead URLs and DOIs:** web fetch was not permitted. The two Hugging Face URLs, the arXiv DOI `10.48550/arXiv.2604.07729` and every other DOI are unverified. I need fetch permission, or someone to open each link.
- **External author names and quotes:**
  - The Sofroniew/Kauvar/Saunders author list and venue for the Anthropic emotions paper. The bib entry mixes "Transformer Circuits Thread" with an arXiv DOI.
  - The quoted sentence *"can (and does) recall previously cached emotion representations…"*.
  - The middle initial in "Winnie N. Street".
  - The Strachan co-authors.

  All unverified. I need the primary pages.
- **Primary bylines for `lyra2026detecting` and `lyra2026concordance`:** I was not granted read access to `C:\Users\Thomas\Desktop\LiberationLabs\Research` outside this worktree. I need that access, or the path to those papers' `.tex`.
- **Whole-PDF extraction:** running `tools/verify_pdf.py` needed approval I didn't have. I checked rendered pages instead: academic pages 1–3 and flight pages 1 and 18–22. The rest of each PDF was not inspected.
- **Sign-off:** I can't tell whether Thomas has approved the title, either byline, or the academic edition's AI-disclosure wording. I also don't know the target venue's AI-authorship policy, which decides between the options in #3.
- **Implicit-arm numbers:** the 63%, the ρ values and the variance ratio have no code or data in this repo, so they are unverified.
